seccion_2_presentacion.titulo_aprendiz: 2. PRESENTATION — Welcome to the Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura
seccion_2_presentacion.prologo_en:
Before you open this guide, take a breath. You are about to cross a threshold.

Tomorrow morning — in this story, at least — you will arrive at the Terminal de Contenedores in Buenaventura. The Pacific air is salty. A gantry crane is moving above you. Someone hands you a hard hat and a VHF radio and points to the berth where the BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS is mooring. They say, in English: 'Trainee, can you confirm the call sign?' You will answer. And in that moment, you will become a Port Operations Trainee.

This guide is the rehearsal. Twelve sessions. One hundred hours. Twenty essential words. Five SMCP standard responses. Five occupational structures. One final mission — coordinating the CML CARRIER turnaround in front of Capitán Restrepo and an external panel.

Let's begin.
seccion_2_presentacion.prologo_es_support:
(Antes de abrir esta guía, respira. Estás a punto de cruzar un umbral.

Mañana — al menos dentro de esta historia — llegarás al Terminal de Contenedores en Buenaventura. El aire del Pacífico es salado. Una grúa pórtico se mueve sobre tu cabeza. Alguien te entrega un casco y una radio VHF y te señala el muelle donde el BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS está atracando. Te dicen, en inglés: 'Trainee, ¿puedes confirmar el call sign?' Tú responderás. Y en ese momento te convertirás en Port Operations Trainee.

Esta guía es el ensayo. Doce sesiones. Cien horas. Veinte palabras esenciales. Cinco respuestas SMCP estándar. Cinco estructuras ocupacionales. Una misión final — coordinar el turnaround del CML CARRIER frente al Capitán Restrepo y un panel externo.

Empecemos.)
seccion_2_presentacion.que_aprenderas_en:
In this guide, you will learn how to operate in English inside a Colombian Pacific port. Over twelve sessions, you will build a professional vocabulary of 20 essential maritime terms across four sub-blocks (Ship Parts & Port Infrastructure · SMCP Standard Phrases · Port Operations · Occupational Structures). You will learn the SMCP standard responses (Roger · Wilco · Affirmative · Negative · Standby) and the NATO Phonetic Alphabet for spelling call signs. You will read technical reports about vessels, write Inspection Reports and Berthing Memos, listen to VHF dialogues filled with real interference, and speak with non-native vessel masters via radio. The guide closes with the CML Port Turnaround Mission — a three-hour condensed simulation in front of Capitán Restrepo.

It is not about speaking perfect English. It is about speaking with operational clarity, the way a trainee at the Buenaventura terminal must.
seccion_2_presentacion.que_aprenderas_es_supervivencia: (En esta guía aprenderás a operar en inglés dentro de un puerto del Pacífico colombiano. A lo largo de doce sesiones construirás un vocabulario profesional de 20 términos marítimos esenciales distribuidos en cuatro sub-bloques (Partes del buque e infraestructura portuaria · Frases SMCP estándar · Operaciones portuarias · Estructuras ocupacionales). Aprenderás las respuestas SMCP estándar y el alfabeto fonético OTAN para deletrear call signs. Leerás reportes técnicos sobre buques, escribirás Inspection Reports y Berthing Memos, escucharás diálogos VHF con interferencia real, y hablarás con vessel masters no-nativos por radio. La guía cierra con la Misión Final CML Port Turnaround — una simulación condensada de 3 horas frente al Capitán Restrepo. No se trata de hablar inglés perfecto. Se trata de hablar con claridad operativa, como debe hacerlo un trainee en el terminal de Buenaventura.)
para_que_te_servira: Reading — When you open a manifesto, an OMI manual, or a SMCP reference card and see technical English everywhere — 'mooring lines,' 'cargo discharge,' 'berthing window' — you will not freeze. You will recognize these terms and keep working. (Cuando abras un manifiesto, un manual OMI o una tarjeta SMCP y veas inglés técnico, no te congelarás — los reconocerás y seguirás trabajando.)

Listening — When Captain Lopera radios in from the bridge with his Singaporean accent and says 'Vessel inbound, request berthing instructions,' you will know exactly what he means and what to answer. (Cuando Captain Lopera te llame por radio con su acento singapurense y diga frases así, sabrás qué quiere decir y cómo responder.)

Writing — When you write your first Inspection Report or Berthing Coordination Memo, it will read like a real Port Trainee wrote it: precise, technical, structured. (Cuando escribas tu primer Inspection Report o Berthing Memo, se leerá como si lo hubiera escrito un Port Trainee real.)

Speaking — When the panel asks 'You're responsible for yard coordination, aren't you?' you will answer with a complete tag-question response. You will not improvise; you will deliver. (Cuando el panel te pregunte con tag question, responderás con una respuesta completa. No improvisarás, entregarás.)

Workplace — And the day your first VHF call comes from a real container vessel arriving from Asia, you will not panic. You will respond. That is, in the end, why this matters. (Y el día que tu primera llamada VHF venga de un buque real arribando de Asia, no entrarás en pánico — responderás. Al final, por eso importa todo esto.)

universo_narrativo_aprendiz.escena_apertura_en:
It is 6:00 a.m. on a Monday at the Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura. The Pacific tide is rising. A gantry crane stands silhouetted against the sky. You climb the steel stairs to the operations office above Berth 4. The door says PORT OPERATIONS · TRAINEE WELCOME. You push it open.

Inside: a wall of monitors showing vessel positions. A laminated SMCP reference card on every desk. A framed photo of Capitán Restrepo shaking hands with the Port Authority. The smell of strong coffee and salt air. A VHF radio crackles somewhere with a call sign in NATO Phonetic.

This is where you will work for the next twelve sessions. Welcome.
universo_narrativo_aprendiz.escena_apertura_es_support: (Son las 6:00 a.m. de un lunes en el Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura. La marea del Pacífico está subiendo. Una grúa pórtico se recorta contra el cielo. Subes las escaleras de acero hacia la oficina de operaciones sobre el Berth 4. La puerta dice PORT OPERATIONS · TRAINEE WELCOME. La empujas. Adentro: una pared de monitores mostrando posiciones de buques. Una tarjeta SMCP plastificada en cada escritorio. Una foto enmarcada del Capitán Restrepo saludando a la Autoridad Portuaria. Olor a café fuerte y aire salado. Una radio VHF crepita en algún lugar con un call sign en alfabeto fonético OTAN. Aquí vas a trabajar durante las próximas doce sesiones. Bienvenido/a.)
universo_narrativo_aprendiz.tu_terminal: Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura — el principal puerto del Pacífico colombiano. Cargo handling 24/7. Vessels internacionales arribando desde Shanghai, Manzanillo, Buenaventura outbound a Callao y Guayaquil. (El principal puerto del Pacífico colombiano.)
universo_narrativo_aprendiz.tu_rol: You are Andrea Mosquera. Port Operations Trainee. 22 years old. Recent SENA graduate. Today is your first real day on the job. You have a freshly-issued hard hat, a SMCP Reference Card laminated in your pocket, a notebook where you have already written down 'bollard' and 'crane' in NATO Phonetic, and — although nobody needs to know this yet — a slightly shaky hand as you pick up the VHF for the first time. That is completely normal. (Eres Andrea Mosquera, Port Operations Trainee, 22 años, recién egresada SENA. Hoy es tu primer día real en el puerto. Tienes un casco nuevo, una tarjeta SMCP plastificada en el bolsillo, un cuaderno donde ya escribiste 'bollard' y 'crane' en alfabeto OTAN, y — aunque nadie tiene que saberlo todavía — la mano un poco temblorosa al levantar el VHF por primera vez. Es completamente normal.)
tu_equipo: Capitán Restrepo — Port Captain. 50+ years. Your direct mentor and evaluator. B1 technical English. He hired you. He will sign your final certificate. You will learn more from his silences than from his instructions. (Port Captain, mentor directo, evaluador panel S12. Aprenderás más de sus silencios que de sus instrucciones.)

Captain Lopera — Vessel Master of the BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS and later of the CML CARRIER. Chinese-Singaporean. 45 years old. He speaks English as a lingua franca — not native, but functional B1. He represents every real vessel master you will meet in your career. He is on the VHF; you will hear him before you see him. (Vessel master · cliente externo permanente · representa el inglés real no-nativo del sector.)

Officer Vásquez — Deck Officer of the BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS. He gives you the tour of the bridge in Session 3. Patient. Speaks slowly. Knows every part of the ship. (Deck Officer · cameo Bloque 1 · te lleva al puente del buque en S3.)

Diego Mejía — Crane Operator at Berth 4. Spanish L1 dominant. Twelve years on the gantry crane. When Diego says a container will not stack, it will not stack. Listen to him. (Crane operator · L1 español · 12 años en la grúa pórtico. Escúchalo.)

Bosun Romero — Yard Supervisor. Spanish L1 dominant. Coordinates mooring lines and yard movements. He is your tripartite partner in Session 8 berthing simulation. (Yard supervisor · L1 español · partner tripartito en S8.)

seccion_2_presentacion.promesa_pedagógica:
Here is what we promise — and what we will hold you to.

Twelve sessions from now, you will walk back into the Terminal de Contenedores and you will not be the same person who opened this guide. You will pick up the VHF without hesitating. You will spell a call sign in NATO Phonetic without looking at the card. You will stand in front of Capitán Restrepo and an external naval agent — Mission Portfolio in your hand, voice steady — and you will speak for three minutes about the CML CARRIER turnaround in English. The panel will ask two questions with tag questions. You will answer with full tag-question responses.

And then, walking out of the terminal that evening, you will know something that nobody can take away from you: I am a Port Operations Trainee — and I can work in this language too. (En doce sesiones volverás al Terminal de Contenedores y no serás la misma persona que abrió esta guía. Levantarás el VHF sin dudar. Deletrearás un call sign en alfabeto OTAN sin mirar la tarjeta. Te pararás frente al Capitán Restrepo y un agente naviero externo — Mission Portfolio en mano, voz firme — y hablarás tres minutos en inglés sobre el turnaround del CML CARRIER. Y esa noche, saliendo del terminal, sabrás algo que nadie puede quitarte: soy Port Operations Trainee, y también puedo trabajar en este idioma.)

You will write a single English word about it: a color, a part, an action. This is your soft opening to maritime English. It matters because the language begins with what you actually see at a real Pacific port; you will not memorize abstract terms, you will name what is in front of you. By the end, you will have your first English maritime word on the table — and the word of a partner next to it.

Al cerrar, tienes tu primera palabra marítima en la tabla y la palabra de un compañero al lado.

contenido_inline.text_en:
Andrea is a Port Operations Trainee at the Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura. Today is Monday. She is at Berth 4 with Officer Vásquez. The vessel is the BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS. It is a container ship from Asia.

The bow is at the front. The stern is at the back. The bridge is on the upper deck. The hull is in the water. The mast is tall and tall.

There are six bollards near the vessel. The mooring lines are secured. A gantry crane is above the deck. The crane is operational.

Captain Lopera is on the bridge. He has a VHF radio. He speaks in SMCP. He says: 'Roger. Standby. Out.' He uses NATO Phonetic to spell the call sign.

The cargo is in the containers. The containers are stacked on the deck. Officer Vásquez says: 'The vessel is at berth 4. The anchor is up. Cargo handling starts in ten minutes.'

Andrea writes this in her notebook: 'BUENAVENTURA EXPRESS · Berth 4 · ETA arrived. Captain Lopera is responsible for the bridge. I report to Capitán Restrepo.'

the_mission.headline_en: 🎯 THE MISSION — Welcome to Your Final Day at the Terminal
the_mission.scenario_en: Today is your day. You are Andrea Mosquera, Port Operations Trainee at the Terminal de Contenedores Buenaventura. You arrived twelve weeks ago — you did not know what a bollard was. Now you do. Capitán Restrepo has assigned you a real mission: the CML CARRIER turn-around. The vessel is arriving from Shanghai. 220 meters LOA. 33-meter beam. 2.500 TEU. ETA 06:15. ETD 18:15. 1.800 containers to discharge. 1.600 to load. Berth 4. Tide window 06:00 to 19:00. Captain Lopera is the Vessel Master — he speaks English as a lingua franca. Diego is on the crane. Bosun Romero is on the yard. You are in the middle. You coordinate. You communicate. You report.

the_briefing.headline: 📋 THE BRIEFING — What Capitán Restrepo + the panel expect from you:
lista: 1. A complete Mission Portfolio: Berthing Coordination Memo (1 page) + Radio Log (5 entries) + Post-Turn Report (incident analysis).
2. VHF Intake response with Captain Lopera in 90 seconds: SMCP standard phrases (Roger · Wilco · Standby · Over) + NATO Phonetic spelling of pilot call sign Papa-Whiskey-Two-Three.

3. Berthing Coordination Tripartite in 2 minutes: simultaneously coordinate Diego (crane · Spanish L1) + Bosun Romero (yard · Spanish L1) + Captain Lopera (VHF · English lingua franca) using modals + conditional 1 + present perfect + passive voice + tag questions.
4. Post-Turn Report oral in 90 seconds to Capitán Restrepo: passive voice past + occupational structures + tag question.
5. Professional Pitch in 3 minutes before the panel (Capitán Restrepo + external naval agent): 4 sections (intro 30s + habitual 60s + momentary 60s + closing tag 30s).
6. Be ready for 2 panel questions with tag questions and respond with active production.

the_deliverable.format_options: Format: (a) Berthing Coordination Memo 1 page A4 + (b) Radio Log 5 entries (table 6 columns) + (c) Post-Turn Report 1 page A4. Submitted physical OR PDF before S12 SET-UP.

✅ Post-Turn Report 1 page · passive voice past + 1 conditional 1 + 1 occupational structure + 1 tag question closing.
✅ Audio Pitch 3 min recorded for personal portfolio (USB delivered S12 close).
